definitions.explanation: Words or phrases chanted to invoke magical or supernatural effects. Used both in traditional religious/spiritual contexts and in modern fantasy, games, and popular culture.

examples.japanese: {魔法使|まほうつか}いが{呪文|じゅもん}を{唱|とな}えた。
{呪文|じゅもん}を{覚|おぼ}えないと{魔法|まほう}は{使|つか}えない。
examples.english: You can't use magic unless you memorize the spells.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちは{呪文|じゅもん}のような{言葉|ことば}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}しながら{遊|あそ}んでいた。
examples.english: The children were playing while repeating words like magic spells.

notes:
Very commonly encountered in RPGs, fantasy anime/manga, and games (especially the Dragon Quest series, where {呪文|じゅもん} is the standard term for spells). Also used in traditional Buddhist and Shinto contexts for sacred chants and incantations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{呪文|じゅもん}を{唱|とな}える — to chant a spell
・{呪文|じゅもん}を{覚|おぼ}える — to learn/memorize a spell
・{呪文|じゅもん}を{解|と}く — to break a spell
・{呪文|じゅもん}のような — spell-like, incomprehensible (like magic words)
